subject: 5-Bullet Friday — 25 Helpful Principles, My Favorite Audiobook in Years, Einstein on Awe and Mystery, and More

bullets.title: 25 Principles of Adult Behavior
bullets.creator: John Perry Barlow
bullets.note:
. John was a lyricist for the Grateful Dead and a founding member of the Electronic Frontier Foundation and the Freedom of the Press Foundation. Many bullets will seem obvious, but a few of them found me at the right time and really resonated:  
​  
​_Avoid the pursuit of happiness. Seek to define your mission and pursue that.  
​_**​  
​**_Become less suspicious of joy._

bullets.section: Audiobook I’ve fallen in love with
bullets.title: When We Cease to Understand the World
bullets.creator: Benjamín Labatut
bullets.note:
. This is probably my favorite book of the last two years. The prose is gorgeous, and it reads as if your favorite biography and a fever dream had a love child. I’ve never encountered such a wellspring of rich historical accuracy and mind-bending imagination. It was first recommended to me by an iconic filmmaker, and I pushed it off, thinking to myself, “If I can’t separate the fact from the fiction, what’s the point?”  
​  
I was perhaps missing the point. First, I think the separation is pretty obvious. Second, you should read this book for the pure joy of it.  
​  
It was selected as one of _The New York Times Book Review_’s 10 Best Books of 2021 and shortlisted for the 2021 International Booker Prize and the 2021 National Book Award for Translated Literature. Here’s the description: “A fictional examination of the lives of real-life scientists and thinkers whose discoveries resulted in moral consequences beyond their imagining. _When We Cease to Understand the World_ is a book about the complicated links between scientific and mathematical discovery, madness, and destruction.”

bullets.title: American Fiction
bullets.note: _American Fiction_ is probably my favorite movie of the last 1–2 years. I’ve become obsessed with it, and you’ll laugh your ass off. It’s a comedic Trojan Horse of epic proportions. Don’t trust the streaming descriptions; _American Fiction_ is about much more. Every character is flawed in their own beautiful, human way, and the writing hits a home run. Ambiguities are left in so that the movie becomes your own Rorschach test. It currently has a 96% audience score on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/american_fiction), and you can find the trailer [here](https://youtu.be/i0MbLCpYJPA?si=Ug0sjjN0n9Q5KMbi). Trust me and watch the trailer.
